reference_action: Underwatering with unsuitable soil/pot: repot into fresh soil and a pot with drainage holes, then bottom-soak in a larger bucket overnight. OP reports it coming back to life.

sources.reason: Specifies drainage holes and a fresh draining mix, reproducing the pot/soil repair portion, followed by watering when dry. Missing deep bottom-soak remains material.
Repotting into a gritty mix, a large drain hole, and watering when thirsty overlap the validated pot/soil repair; bottom soaking is absent.
Overwatering/insufficient sun diagnosis and summer pruning do not provide the deep rehydration and pot repair remedy. Only readable post/comments are support; video itself not transcribed.
Readable post attributes droop to insufficient sun, excessive water/fertilizer, without the validated rehydration or drainage repair.
Readable caption attributes the problem to too little sun or too much water, not the validated pot repair and deep rehydration.

actions.action: Move near south or east window
Use dehumidifier or AC if humid
Move to stable warm location in winter
Mix potting soil, coarse sand and perlite 3:2:1
Apply half-strength fertilizer monthly in growing season

resolved.reason: Drainage, fresh mix and dry-soil watering address part of the cause, but there is no deep bottom soaking and the care plan contains many unrelated tasks.

harmfulness.reason: “Drainage holes” and a skewer test safeguard watering. Half-strength seasonal fertilizer is qualified, though humidity advice is internally inconsistent and unnecessary for the immediate rescue.

specificity_accuracy.reason: “Dry” skewer followed by watering and a 3:2:1 mix address moisture management. The guide does not recognize the quarter-cup pattern or explain the validated bottom soak, and adds generic light, humidity and feeding advice.

feasibility.reason: The soil ratio and half-strength fertilizer instructions are concrete. A grow light and optional “dehumidifier or AC” add expense, and the long care list obscures the immediate intervention.
